nodes.statement: Fix one unoriented binary structural coordinate Z, three comparison populations and two marker-channel polarity variables per population; actual bearers, intervals, lineage, installation, use, measurement and admission remain distinct sorts.
nodes.scope: Seven Boolean sign variables in one declared comparison design; not a complete organization or token admission.
nodes.quantifier: For every labelling of the seven fixed variables.

nodes.statement: Encode cross-population correspondences and prospective marker reversals as fixed XOR parity edges without assigning familiar-mineness semantics to either pole.
nodes.scope: Finite signed graphs over the R194 domain.
nodes.quantifier: For every declared equality or reversal edge.

nodes.statement: Every cycle-consistent signed graph has 2^c compatible labellings for c unanchored connected components; one fixed vertex per component gives one numeric labelling, while an inconsistent cycle gives none.
nodes.quantifier: For every finite signed graph in the declared class.

nodes.statement: Multiple populations, markers and known reversal relations can identify relative channel polarity and connect components.
nodes.scope: The declared signed comparison design, conditional on correct edges and same-target transport.

nodes.statement: Without an oriented anchor, every connected component retains a simultaneous global-complement mate; relative alignment therefore does not identify the familiar-mineness pole.
nodes.scope: Evidence packages invariant under simultaneous Boolean complement.
nodes.quantifier: For every compatible unanchored connected component.

nodes.statement: Relational anchors, conventional code anchors and substantively target-directed anchors are different: only the last can conditionally warrant phenomenal orientation.
nodes.scope: R194 polarity claims and future bodily/action-mineness applications.

nodes.statement: A familiar-mineness polarity anchor must be prospective, independently target-directed, falsifiable, reliable and applicable to the same actually installed and used organizational slice.
nodes.scope: The named familiar embodied/action-mineness target, not basal experience.

nodes.statement: Nonreport status, marker positivity, test success, actual route use and named experience remain distinct; tests are evidence and do not install use or define experience.
nodes.scope: One bound bodily/action marker protocol without an added reliability and admission bridge.
nodes.quantifier: For every tested marker channel and token application.

nodes.statement: Future polarity work must separately discharge relative alignment, substantive semantic orientation, actual organization/use, measurement reliability and token admission.
nodes.scope: UCT familiar bodily/action-mineness research; no basal-experience gate or unique owner.
nodes.quantifier: For every future named-target application using population or marker alignment.

rules.statement: Propagate parity from one root per component under all simultaneous fixed-edge and transport constraints.
rules.binding: The graph, vertices, edge parities and coordinate interpretation remain fixed throughout one enumeration.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: No alternative route; cycle consistency and component structure are simultaneous premises.

rules.statement: Use connected consistent parity relations to identify channel correspondences without assigning target semantics.
rules.binding: All marker channels are asserted to concern the same transported comparison target; actual truth remains open.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: Disconnected components retain independent sign freedoms.

rules.statement: Apply simultaneous Boolean complement to every vertex in an unanchored connected component.
rules.binding: Only sign labels change; organization, graph, edge parities and evidence remain fixed.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: A target-directed oriented anchor is intentionally absent.

rules.statement: Separate code-fixing from target-semantic warrant and record the still-open substantive anchor premise.
rules.binding: The marker convention and named phenomenal target are kept as different sorts on the same proposed application.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: A conventional anchor yields one numeric code but no B_fam derivation.

rules.statement: Keep actual history and present use distinct from nonreport marker evidence and test success.
rules.binding: History requires actual occurrence, lineage and continuation; use requires the actual present consumer; markers remain evidence.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: A reliability bridge can support inference but cannot redefine actual use as test success.

rules.statement: Combine relative identification, polarity nonidentification, anchor typing, evidence separation and the inherited open target boundary.
rules.binding: Formal alignment, phenomenal semantics, actual relation membership and token evidence remain separate evidence grades.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: No individual premise independently yields the protocol or B_fam.

context_links.statement: R194 supplies a finite signed instance inside the established representation/fiber discipline.
A transported and aligned coordinate is not thereby correctly named familiar mineness.
Copied values and positive tests do not establish same-lineage retention or current use.
No marker, population comparison, anchor or familiar-mineness bridge is required for basal nonempty experience.
C1 remains a project axiom; the polarity theorem neither proves nor replaces it.
